answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a time-locked stake vault: a new identity must lock a deposit that unlocks only gradually as peers attest to honest completed work. Copying yourself into many identities then multiplies the locked capital and the waiting time, while a single bad act freezes the whole vault. Reputation grows like yarrow — slowly, from verified roots — and a violet warning flag on a fresh, unproven identity tells counterparties to demand escrow until its history is earned, not merely claimed.
